title: Research (no κ claim): b = ZQY needs ≥ 112 paid jobs per FULL; #5415's exit is optimal; structural-lever obstructions
body:
**No κ claim.** This answers zxv's #5428 target 1 (the encoded-output exit) and screens the other structural levers on the #5413 caller.

**Main theorem.** Every exact, width-uniform producer of **b = Z·Q·Y** from post-return data needs **≥ 112 paid jobs per backward FULL**. The bound holds for any rank, any operator and any sharing pattern: butterflies, block transforms, joint diagonalisation and shared higher-rank intermediates are all covered.
- The whole #5415 exit needs ≥ 120, so **#5415's 120-H1 exit is optimal**.
- The break-even is τ = 63.52 H1 per FULL, so this route cannot pass U = 0.00302728825.
- This extends #5427, which shows b is not free, to paid producers.
- The proof uses a coset-span lemma. The 112 coset directions (56 per mode) are computed exactly over ℚ with the repository's `clifford_exact` evaluator, including absolute phase.
- Controls: three sanity targets give 8, 8 and 0; 300 random programs never beat the lemma; making one C gate free breaks it.

**Other levers.**
- Rank-9 helpers have **no free split point** in either orientation (exact replay on all 632 registers).
- A bought exit needs ≥ 15 modes per FULL; the #5402 family has 8.
- A productive centre payload earns 0; query-shear deletion breaks the rank-mass balance; query/local fusion is illegal.
- Defragmentation is closed at a fixed operation set.

**Open.** The only remaining b-route uses a pre-return copy of y: 8×H8 = 63.598 against τ = 63.523, a loss of 0.076 per FULL. That is the centre-interface lever (#4694/#4698/#4700).

Package: `research/encoded-exit-obstructions/` (README, R16/R17 notes, tools, expected outputs). Companion notes: #5465 (reorder/re-frame ceilings) and #5462 (owned-relation optimum).
